### Executive Summary
- Multiple **actively exploited / KEV** paths to takeover internet-facing apps: **Oracle PeopleSoft PeopleTools 0‑day (CVE-2026-35273)** and **Joomla JCE (CVE-2026-48907)**; treat as **ransomware initial access risk**.
- **Microsoft Defender “RoguePlanet” zero-day (CVE-2026-50656)** is public and unpatched (patch pending); expect rapid commoditization for **local privilege escalation** post-compromise.
- AI/OSS ecosystem risk rising: **LiteLLM unauth RCE chain (CVE-2026-42271 + CVE-2026-48710)** and **npm typosquat (easy-day-js)**; combined with reports of **EDR-killer tooling** and **Teams-relayed C2** in ransomware ops.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) Oracle PeopleSoft PeopleTools 0‑day actively exploited (CVE-2026-35273; ransomware-linked)**
- What happened: CISA added a **PeopleSoft PeopleTools unauth takeover 0‑day** to KEV; exploitation tied to ransomware activity.
- Why it matters operationally: Any internet-exposed PeopleSoft tier is a **high-probability initial access vector** leading to domain compromise/ransomware.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Identify/confirm PeopleSoft exposure** (external + internal), prioritize emergency patch/mitigation; **hunt for anomalous web/app admin actions** and new webshell-like artifacts on PeopleSoft servers.

**2) Joomla Content Editor (JCE) max-severity exploit in the wild (CVE-2026-48907; KEV)**
- What happened: CISA added **Joomla JCE** CVE-2026-48907 (CVSS 10) to KEV; reports indicate **automated exploitation**.
- Why it matters operationally: Common CMS foothold → rapid **credential theft / webshell / lateral movement**; orgs often have “forgotten” Joomla instances.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Scan for Joomla/JCE** across DMZ and marketing domains; **block/alert on suspicious POST/extension upload patterns** and validate patching/removal of JCE where not needed.

**3) Microsoft Defender “RoguePlanet” zero-day (CVE-2026-50656) – patch pending**
- What happened: Microsoft confirmed **Defender local elevation-of-privilege** zero-day; patch is in development (no fix yet).
- Why it matters operationally: If an attacker gets code execution as a user, this can help them **escalate privileges**, disable defenses, and stage ransomware faster.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Increase alerting for privilege escalation + tamper attempts** on endpoints; **tighten application control** where feasible (block untrusted binaries/scripts from user-writable paths).

**4) AI/Dev tooling exposure: LiteLLM unauth RCE chain + supply-chain typosquat (easy-day-js)**
- What happened: **LiteLLM MCP test endpoints command injection (CVE-2026-42271)** can become **unauth RCE** when chained with **Starlette host-header bypass (CVE-2026-48710)**; separate report flags **easy-day-js npm typosquat** impacting AI framework dependencies.
- Why it matters operationally: Financial orgs increasingly run AI gateways internally; compromise risks **API key/LLM connector credential theft** and pivot into cloud/SaaS.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Inventory LiteLLM deployments** and upgrade (**LiteLLM 1.83.7 + Starlette 1.0.1**) and **rotate credentials** the gateway accessed (per guidance); **flag new/unknown npm packages** in builds, and quarantine builds pulling `easy-day-js`.

**5) Ransomware tradecraft updates: Teams-relayed C2 + “EDR killer” tooling**
- What happened: Reporting shows ransomware (e.g., **DragonForce**) using **Microsoft Teams infrastructure as C2 relay** for weeks; separate reporting highlights **Gentlemen/GentleKiller-style EDR disabling** tooling targeting many security products.
- Why it matters operationally: Network-based C2 detection may miss **legitimate cloud relay traffic**; EDR-killers can reduce visibility right before encryption/exfiltration.
- Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today: **Baseline Teams traffic** (endpoints/processes initiating) and alert on **Teams used by unusual processes**; prioritize triage of **security service stop/disable events** as potential pre-ransomware signals.

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **PeopleSoft / web app exploitation**: WAF/reverse-proxy + app logs for PeopleSoft servers; hunt for **new admin users, unexpected PeopleTools actions, unusual JSP/PS app file writes** (ATT&CK: T1190).
- **Joomla/JCE exploitation**: Web server logs for Joomla sites; alert on **extension/component upload attempts, unusual POSTs to editor endpoints, spikes in 4xx/5xx** around admin paths (T1190, T1505.003).
- **Defender RoguePlanet LPE signals**: EDR + Windows Security logs; hunt for **privilege escalation chains** (new local admins, token manipulation, abnormal service creation) (T1068, T1543.003).
- **EDR tampering / “killer” behavior**: EDR telemetry + Windows event logs for **service stop/disable**, driver install attempts, registry changes to security tooling, and **tamper protection events** (T1562.001).
- **Teams-relayed C2**: Proxy/DNS + Microsoft 365/Defender for Cloud Apps logs; alert on **Teams network connections initiated by non-Teams binaries**, and unusual outbound volume/session duration from servers that don’t use Teams (T1071.001).
- **LiteLLM/Starlette exploitation**: API gateway logs + container/K8s audit logs; hunt for **requests to MCP test endpoints**, suspicious Host headers, and **command execution inside pods** (T1190, T1059).
- **Supply-chain (npm) ingestion**: CI/CD logs + artifact repo + EDR on build agents; alert on **new dependency names similar to popular libs** and unexpected postinstall scripts (T1195.001).
- **Cloud logging abuse (visibility evasion)**: Cloud control plane logs (AWS CloudTrail / Azure Activity / GCP Audit); watch for **logging configuration changes**, new sinks/exports, or deletion of log resources (T1562.008).

---

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Patch/workaround tracking**: Prepare for rapid deployment of the **Defender CVE-2026-50656** patch when released; pre-stage change windows and validation tests.
- **External attack surface review**: Ensure continuous discovery of **forgotten Joomla/PeopleSoft** and other legacy web apps; enforce ownership and patch SLAs for internet-facing services.
- **AI gateway hardening**: For LiteLLM/AI proxies, standardize: **disable test/debug endpoints**, restrict admin interfaces, enforce mTLS/IP allowlists, and maintain **credential rotation runbooks**.
- **Supply-chain governance**: Tighten controls for npm/PyPI/containers (allowlists, lockfiles, SCA gating, signed artifacts) and add an escalation path when typosquats are detected.
- **Ransomware prep**: Validate alert coverage for **defense evasion + credential access**; run a tabletop focused on **EDR tamper + cloud-relayed C2** scenarios.
- **Fortinet/FortiBleed context (assumption-based)**: If we operate Fortinet appliances, validate exposure/credential hygiene and monitor vendor advisories; treat any credential leak claims as **rotate + review remote access** triggers.
